title: What If You Stood on the Surface of Venus?

scenes.text: What if you stood on the surface of Venus? You'd last far less time than a robot.
The air alone is about four hundred and sixty-five degrees Celsius, hot enough to melt lead.
The pressure is roughly ninety times Earth's, like being almost a kilometre under the sea.
In 1982 the Soviet probe Venera 13 landed there. It was built to last about half an hour.
It kept working for one hundred and twenty-seven minutes and sent back fourteen colour photographs.
That is still the record. Everything we know of Venus's ground came from machines that died within about two hours.

description:
What if you stood on the surface of Venus?
About 465 degrees Celsius and crushing pressure. The longest any lander has survived there is 127 minutes.
